abstract: Surgical intervention is essential for choledochal cysts (CCs) due to their high lifetime risk of progressing to cholangiocarcinoma, yet management strategies vary worldwide. Given bile fluid's vital role in digestion, investigating bile flow dynamics may provide surgeons with additional insights for treatment planning. In this study, one MRI-based healthy adult scan was used to reconstruct biliary system, which was then modified according to Todani classifications to generate eight CC types. Particle Image Velocimetry was used to first visualize local velocity field, followed by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations of bile emptying to analyze pathological non-Newtonian bile flow. Wall shear stress (WSS), a key biomechanical parameter, was visualized through 2D surface mapping for comparative evaluation. Results showed consistently low velocity in dilated regions, suggesting bile accumulation in CCs, particularly in Types 1a, 2, 4a, and 4b. While WSS changes were minimal in the healthy biliary system, extreme gradients, up to 10,000-fold emerged in CCs, especially Types 1a, 2, and 4a. These findings highlight that bile flow characteristics are primarily dictated by localized anatomical abnormalities, aligning with surgical interventions that target dilated regions. These findings demonstrate the potential of CFD to provide additional biomechanical insights into bile flow abnormalities associated with different CC types, which may serve as a reference for future clinical investigations.
